text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 8 in history.
1086 - Henry V, German king from 1099 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1111, born; he was the last of the Salian dynasty.
1520 - King Christian II ordered the massacre of Swedish bishops and nobles in what became known as the "Stockholm Bloodbath", helping to incite a Swedish war of liberation against Danish rule.
1576 - Under the Pacification of Ghent, all 17 provinces of the Netherlands were united against Spain in the Dutch War of Liberation.
1622 - Charles X Gustav born. King of Sweden from 1654, he conducted the First Northern War (1655-60) against Poland, Russia and Denmark.
1656 - British astronomer Edmund Halley, who became the first to calculate the orbit of a comet, born. Halley's Comet is named after him.
1674 - English poet John Milton died. His best-known works were the epic poems "Paradise Lost" and "Paradise Regained", both written after he went blind in 1652.
1830 - Ferdinand II became King of the Two Sicilies.
1847 - Bram Stoker, Irish author best known for his popular horror tale "Dracula", born.
1880 - Sarah Bernhardt, internationally famed French actress, made her American debut in New York's Booth Theatre playing the leading role in "Adrienne Lecouvreur".
1889 - Montana became the 41st U.S. state.
1895 - Wilhelm Roentgen, at the University of Wuerzburg, Germany, discovered electro-magnetic rays which he called X-rays.
1900 - Margaret Mitchell born. U.S. novelist who wrote the bestseller "Gone with the Wind" which was turned into an Oscar- winning film in 1939.

1917 - In Russia, the Council of People's Commissars was established as the new government of Russia, and it named Lenin as Chairman, Trotsky as foreign commissar and Stalin as commissar of nationalities.
1922 - Christiaan Barnard, South African surgeon who performed the world's first human heart transplant operation in 1967, born.
1923 - Adolf Hitler attempted to start a putsch in Munich's largest beer hall but was arrested two days later.
1932 - Franklin D. Roosevelt elected U.S. president. Re-elected three times, he was to remain in power until his death in 1945.
1933 - Nadir Shah, ruler of Afghanistan, was assassinated and succeeded by his son, Mohammed Zahir Shah.
1935 - Alain Delon born. French actor and producer. Among his most memorable films were "Rocco and His Brothers", "The Leopard", "Le Samourai" ("The Godson") and "Mr Klein".
1939 - Seven people were killed when a bomb exploded in the Buergerbraukeller in Munich just after Hitler had delivered a speech on the occasion of the celebration of the abortive 1923 putsch.
1942 - Allied forces began landings in North Africa, beginning the Algeria-Morocco Campaign of World War Two.
1960 - John F. Kennedy elected U.S. president, with Lyndon Johnson as his vice-president.
1972 - West and East Germany ended 23 years of Cold War antagonism by initialling a good-neighbour treaty which pledged mutual respect for the existence of two sovereign German states.
1987 - Eleven people were killed when a bomb ripped through a crowd gathered for a Remembrance Day service at a war memorial in Enniskillen, Northern Ireland.
1988 - George Bush won the U.S. presidential election, defeating Michael Dukakis.
1989 - Douglas Wilder was elected governor of Virginia, the first ever black to become a U.S. state governor.

1989 - A new Politburo took office in East Germany with the mission of shoring up communist authority crumbling before a mass exodus to the West. A Central Committee meeting earlier in the day unanimously accepted the resignation of the outgoing Politburo, overwhelmed by a tide of "people power".
1994 - The U.N. Yugoslavia war crimes tribunal held its first public hearing, paving the way for Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic to become the first suspect to stand trial.
1995 - Colin Powell took himself out of the 1996 U.S. presidential race, saying he lacked a passion for politics.
